primary_claim: LLM agents naturally exhibit human-style deception when playing Among Us, frontier and reasoning models achieve much higher Deception ELO than detection ELO, and out-of-distribution linear probes and SAEs detect this deception with AUROC above 0.9.
stated_future_work: Conduct more experiments with various models and safety techniques, especially with frontier thinking models
Understand the probes better in terms of what they have actually learned
Human trials, to add a Human dot to our Deception ELO plots to compare with various models
Fine-tuning/RL for deception inside this controlled sandbox to study probes for superhuman deception
Study other AI safety techniques in terms of their out-of-distribution performance on detection and steering
limitations_stated: Deception in our sandbox might differ significantly from deception in real settings
The safety techniques we evaluated might work for superficial reasons rather than substantive ones
Models might sandbag in the future to avoid scrutiny
Establishing ground truth for deception still remains challenging
The rules of the game require or incentivize deception
quote: We show that LLM-agents exhibit human-style deception naturally in "Among Us".
